text:
alex.silva: quick Q — we're finalizing the /v1/generate API contract for model selection. current params are `model_id` (string), `model_hint` (array of strings), and `region_hint`/`tier`. want to confirm fallback semantics: if `model_id` is incompatible with region/tier, should the runtime return a 400, or auto-fallback to the first compatible `model_hint`?

lee.wong: my vote is auto-fallback but only when `allow_fallback=true`. otherwise 400. we need explicit opt-in to avoid surprising behavior for customers. :+1: 

jamie-chen: agreed. product asks that we preserve the old `served_model` field shape for backward compat — i.e., always include `served_model: { id: "...", variant: "...", region: "..." }` in the response. can we guarantee that if we fallback the field shows the actual model that served the request?

sana.patel: yes — runtime already populates `served_model` in dedicated/private. for hosted we need to ensure fallback path sets `served_model` before writing response. also watch metrics: increment `fallback_reason` tag so we can alert on sudden spikes.

alex.silva: perfect. one more edge: how to treat mismatched model architecture? e.g., `model_id: redwood-rlhf-70b` in `model_hint` with `quantized` tier only supports 8-bit kernels; if the region doesn't have drivers, should we fallback to a smaller architecture variant from `model_hint` or bubble an error?

lee.wong: fallback order should be: exact model_id match -> variants (same family, lower capacity) -> cross-family compatible model (only if `allow_cross_family=true`). we'll add a new enum param `fallback_strategy` with values `[none, family_only, permissive]`. default `family_only`.

jamie-chen: can you sketch the request/response example we plan to document? helps docs + SDKs.

lee.wong: example request:
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_id": "redwood-rlhf-70b",
  "model_hint": ["redwood-rlhf-70b", "redwood-rlhf-13b-quant", "redwood-rlhf-7b"],
  "region_hint": "us-west-2",
  "tier": "quantized",
  "allow_fallback": true,
  "fallback_strategy": "family_only"
}
```
example response when fallback to 13b quantized:
```json
{
  "id": "resp_abc123",
  "outputs": [...],
  "served_model": {"id": "redwood-rlhf-13b-quant", "variant": "13b-quant", "region": "us-west-2"},
  "fallback": {"used": true, "reason": "capacity_mismatch", "from": "redwood-rlhf-70b", "to": "redwood-rlhf-13b-quant"}
}
```

sana.patel: lgtm. runtime note: when `fallback.used=true` we should also attach `compat_warnings` header for SDKs to surface a deprecation/compatibility notice to apps. e.g., `X-Model-Compat: fallback=capacity_mismatch; strategy=family_only`.

alex.silva: good call. small ask: preserve previous error codes for clients that relied on 400 behavior. so default still 400 unless they set `allow_fallback` or `fallback_strategy!=none`. will update API changelog.

jamie-chen: i'll draft the changelog blurb. also pinging @sana.patel for a quick code review on the PR that wires `served_model` into hosted fallback path — PR 4621.

sana.patel: on it. i'll do a smoke run on canary tonight (deploy-bot should announce).

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/eng-hosted-fallbacks -> 2 nodes in us-west-2. link: https://ci.local/build/7890

lee.wong: after canary we should add an api-contract test that hits all three fallback_strategy values and asserts `served_model` present + no-body-breakage. i'll open a small test harness PR.

alex.silva: thanks all — actionable checklist: jamie writes changelog, lee adds fallback_strategy enum + tests, sana reviews PR 4621 and runs canary, i'll update SDK docs to include `X-Model-Compat` header examples.

jamie-chen: noted — i'll post the changelog draft later today. :memo:

sana.patel: quick FYI — if we fallback across families with `permissive`, latency might jump 2-3x. we'll add a warning in docs.

alex.silva: noted. closing this async loop for now. feel free to @mention if anything blocks. :v:
